newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac reaffirms France wants Poland in EU in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Chirac reaffirms France wants Poland in EU in 2000.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac reaffirmed support on Monday for Poland to join the European Union in the year 2000 and for the former communist state to enter NATO.

Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski, on a two-day visit to France, praised Chirac's ideas as "promising and realistic" for Poland. The European Commission reckons that EU enlargement to eastern Europe is unlikely before the year 2002.
"France has adopted a completely clear position in favour of Polish membership of the European Union and NATO," Chirac told reporters after about 90 minutes of talks with Kwasniewski.
"Nothing will happen to change that position," he said, insisting that French foreign policy would be unaffected by a May 25-June 1 parliamentary election.

He said that NATO would issue invitations for the first former Communist countries to join at a summit in Madrid on July 8. France wants Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Romania to be in a first wave of new alliance members.
Referring to the European Union, Chirac said: "If you want what I believe, it's that Poland will be a member in the year 2000. I said it in Warsaw, I am convinced that this will be the reality."
Chirac visited Warsaw last September and made a similar comment. He has expressed similar hopes over the past year that the Czech Republic and Hungary will join the EU at the millennium.
"In any case, France will be at Poland's side in its course towards membership and will support it," Chirac said.
Chirac also proposed setting up a working group of officials from the French and Polish presidencies and representatives of foreign affairs and defence ministries to follow up the EU talks.
Kwasniewski said the proposed group would hold "detailed discussions on problems that may arise on the path of the talks."
Chirac also told Kwasniewski that France was still prepared to stage a summit on May 27 for a treaty binding Russia into a new relationship with NATO after the Cold War.

"France is ready to host the summit if the talks are concluded on time," a French official quoted Chirac as saying. U.S. and Russian officials claimed progress in talks in Moscow last week on resolving remaining obstacles.

French officials said that Franco-Polish trade had expanded by 47 percent in 1996, making France Poland's fifth biggest trading partner. It was the fifth largest source of foreign investment in Poland last year.
